### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **66** documentable anchor(s).

**59** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 98f640d581339769d54cf27c8f7b02cbc46849f4`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `userId (5 routes)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **222** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **159** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **159**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 98f640d581339769d54cf27c8f7b02cbc46849f4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `53baf7d7957badf7c523708da90f3c1097e14262` — the merge of head `36d3a9fd823694d741e71173b38c783753ffdaaf` into base `98f640d581339769d54cf27c8f7b02cbc46849f4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 53baf7d7957badf7c523708da90f3c1097e14262 && git checkout 53baf7d7957badf7c523708da90f3c1097e14262
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 98f640d581339769d54cf27c8f7b02cbc46849f4 36d3a9fd823694d741e71173b38c783753ffdaaf && git checkout -B drift-repro 98f640d581339769d54cf27c8f7b02cbc46849f4 && git merge --no-ff 36d3a9fd823694d741e71173b38c783753ffdaaf

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 98f640d581339769d54cf27c8f7b02cbc46849f4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 98f640d581339769d54cf27c8f7b02cbc46849f4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `842d17a53a2bd4d2fc870203f46a611f23dfd718`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/mcp-token-revocation.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-mcp-access-token.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-request-routing.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/mcp-token-revocation.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.mcp-oauth.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.mcp-verifier-keyring.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.mcp-oauth-resource.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.oauth-consent-organization.test.ts + packages/spec/src/contracts/auth-service.ts (`verifyMcpAccessToken`, main), packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.ts (the MCP door: falsy or thrown verify → anonymous → 401; the ban read outside that net → 503), packages/runtime/src/security/oauth-subject-ban.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-plugin-list.ts (`postLogin.consentReferenceId`, `customAccessTokenClaims`), `@better-auth/oauth-provider` 1.7.12 dist (`revokeEndpoint`, `revokeJwtAccessToken`, `revokeAccessToken`, `revokeRefreshToken`, `extractClientCredentials`, `normalizeClientAuthenticationParameters`, `findConsent`, `invalidateRefreshFamily`, `deleteConsentEndpoint`, `updateConsentEndpoint`, the consent write in the authorize flow, the access-token mint), `@better-auth/core` 1.7.12 `decodeBasicCredentials`. Face: the paths decide none (no schema or governed hit — `record-recognisers --template --paths` on the file list defers to the changeset's `Clause-②:` line, which carries `(narrowing)`), so the floor is every non-prose path of the diff; `.changeset/30345-mcp-token-revocation.md` is prose and is read under ②. Read against merge base `cf478ea3398e90e97e73f421fd7f0842a6bd04bd`. The provider dist was read from the registry tarball of the lockfile's exact version (integrity equal to `pnpm-lock.yaml`), since this checkout carries no `node_modules`.

Check-runs on the head at the time of this record: every completed run is `success` or `skipped`, none `failure`; still `in_progress`: `Test Core (1/8)`, `Test Core (4/8)`. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; this record does not stand in for them.

### ① Derived judgments

The MCP door (`verifyMcpAccessToken`), each change to its accept set, judged against the contract on main and the ruled design:

- A token whose consent for (`azp`, `sub`, `organization_id`) is absent → refused. Right: ruling step 3; the contract's "falsy when … revoked".
- A consent created after the token's `iat` → refused, compared in whole seconds. Right, and exact rather than approximate: the provider writes `createdAt` as `new Date(iat * 1e3)` in the authorize flow and stamps `iat` in whole seconds on every access token it mints, so the two sides are in the same unit; a millisecond compare would refuse a legitimate first token (minted later in the consent's own second). A re-consent updates `scopes`/`updatedAt` and never `createdAt`, so a standing grant keeps admitting its tokens.
- No `azp` → refused before any read. Right as fail-closed (the read has no key); the provider mints `azp` on every token and the `IAuthService` principal type is not changed. A declared narrowing beyond the card's own text; carried in the PR body, the changeset and a test.
- No `iat`, or an unreadable `createdAt` → refused. Right (fail closed); the provider always writes both.
- Store error, or no storage adapter → refused. Right: ruling step 3 "fail closed on a store error".
- `skip_consent` client with no consent row → admitted after a second read (`oauthClient`). Right: step 5; the second read runs only on a consent miss, so the consenting client's cost stays at one read. No built-in client in `plugin-auth` sets `skipConsent`; DCR cannot set it.
- Organization keying: the token's claim is minted from the consent's `referenceId` (carried on the code and the refresh family, `customAccessTokenClaims`), so (`azp`, `sub`, claim) names exactly the consent row that authorized it; a token with no claim reads the row with no reference, as the provider's own `findConsent` does. A token minted for one organization presented under another changes nothing here: the read keys on the token, and the resolver already vets the claim against membership.

The revoke door (`/oauth2/revoke`), each change:

- `400 unsupported_token_type` → the wrap verifies the token as this deployment's MCP access token (`verifyMcpAccessTokenClaims`: signature, issuer, MCP audience, delegated subject), reads the authenticated client in the provider's own order (assertion `sub`/`iss`, else `Basic` via the same `decodeBasicCredentials`, else the single form `client_id`; a repeated or mixed shape falls back to the provider's answer, and the provider itself refuses mixed methods) and acts only when `azp` equals it: delete the consent for (client, user, organization), delete the refresh family for (client, user) and the opaque access rows bound to it, answer 200. Right: step 1; the provider's client authentication has run first and is not re-done. Another client's token → 200 touching nothing. Right: step 1 and RFC 7009 §2.1. A `skip_consent` client → the provider's 400 stands. Right: step 5.
- `400 invalid_request` with one of the provider's three unknown-token descriptions → 200. Right for an unknown or invalid token (step 4, RFC 7009 §2.2), and the closed list is pinned against the installed dist so a provider bump cannot silently turn a new refusal into a 200. **Wrong on one request shape** (must-fix, ④).
- A refusal the provider makes before it reads the token (no client, unknown client, empty token) passes through. Right.
- A non-form body keeps the provider's 400. Acceptable: RFC 7009 §2.1 requires form encoding.
- A store error while revoking → `500 server_error`, `no-store`, retry completes it. Fail-closed and idempotent (consent first, so the MCP door already refuses when a later step fails). Should-fix: RFC 7009 §2.2.1 names 503 as the shape a client reads as "the token still exists, retry after a delay"; a 500 is not that signal.

Public surface: `mcp-token-revocation.ts` and `auth-manager-mcp-access-token.ts` are not reached from the package entry; `answerOAuthTokenRevocation` is private; the `IAuthService` contract text and the principal type are unchanged. No object, table or gate is added (step 6). The `auth-manager.ts` revocation note is rewritten to the new rule (Acceptance, last bullet).

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/30345-mcp-token-revocation.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-auth` `patch`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, the BREAKING banner and one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), identical on the PR body and the changeset. `patch` is right: the kind is `none` and no authorable key, export or config field moves; `(narrowing)` keeps the breaking banner.

The arm, judged against `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` and the dispatch skill's rule: removing a mis-refusal that published text already negates is itself `no`, and that `no` must cite the text; a deliberate guard, security refusal or fail-closed removed is `yes`. The revoke door's 400 → 200 is the former, and the citation holds: the card's governing text names RFC 7009 §2.2 ("an invalid token answers 200"), and the contract on main promises a `verifyMcpAccessToken` that answers falsy for a *revoked* token, which the provider's `unsupported_token_type` ("cannot be revoked server-side") contradicted once ruling A made revocation real. Neither refusal removed is a ruling guard or a fail-closed path: every fail-closed answer the door had (no client, unknown client, malformed request) is kept. The one surface that shrinks is the MCP door, and the `(narrowing)` arm carries it. So `no (narrowing)` is right; `yes (narrowing)` would read the same level and the same gates.

### ③ Boundary flags

(a) **A consent-store outage answers 401 at the MCP door; the ban read answers 503.** Within the ruling and the contract: step 3 says "fails closed on a store error" and names no status; the contract's only channel is a falsy value, on which the resolver answers anonymous → 401, and its own `catch` around the verifier maps a thrown error to the same outcome, so a 503 is not reachable from inside the verifier at all. Reaching it needs either the branded-class re-raise the ban read uses (`AuthzStoreUnavailableError`, outside the verifier's net) or the consent read placed in the resolver — the ruling's second option for step 3 — both a change to the resolver's declared posture. A 401 here mints no wrong admission: the re-authorize it provokes reads the same store. Escalated to the maintainer as the PR body already does; not a blocker.

(b) **The refresh family is deleted per (client, user) across organizations; the consent delete is per organization.** This is the ruled step 1 verbatim ("revoke the client's refresh family for that user") and the provider's own `invalidateRefreshFamily(clientId, userId)`, which has no organization axis. Accepted. The visible asymmetry: a person consented to the same client in two organizations who revokes one token keeps the other organization's consent and its live access tokens, but loses that organization's refresh tokens and re-connects there on expiry. An accepted cost under ruling A, recorded here, not a defect.

(c) **`update-consent` scope narrowing does not end an already-minted token.** The dev is right that this is outside ruling A: the ruled read keys on the row's existence and `createdAt`, the provider's update touches `scopes` and `updatedAt` only, and a token's scopes are self-contained claims. It is not a breach of the contract on main ("revoked" is not "narrowed"). It is a user-visible gap of its own (a Console scope reduction takes effect at expiry), already noted in the PR's Acceptance notes; the owner seat should file it as its own card rather than leave it in a PR body. Not a blocker.

### ④ Design judgment

- `mcp-token-revocation.ts` — the consent read matches the provider's own `findConsent` rule for the organization reference (exact match with a reference; missing/null/empty without one); the delete order (consent first) makes the partial-failure state safe; `revokeMcpGrant` mirrors `invalidateRefreshFamily` step for step (opaque access rows by `refreshId in`, then the family); `authenticatedClientIdOf` mirrors `extractClientCredentials` and the provider's single-method rule; the wrap runs only after a provider answer and never authenticates a client. Attempts to break it: a confidential client authenticating as itself while naming another client's id in the form falls under the provider's own "one method" refusal or its `Basic`-first order, which the wrap reads identically; a refresh-token replay after revoke finds no row (400 at the token endpoint, pinned); a re-consent after revoke gets a newer `createdAt`, so the old token stays refused (pinned, with the control that the new token is admitted); a mint–revoke–re-consent inside one wall-clock second would re-admit the old token for its lifetime — inherent to the ruled `iat` rule and the provider's whole-second `createdAt`, not fixable in this module, recorded as a known edge; in a multi-node deployment a node clock ahead of the minting node by more than the consent-to-exchange delay refuses legitimate tokens until re-consent — same class, same source, recorded. **One must-fix:** the door answers 200 on a request shape on which the provider has not examined the presented token as an access token at all, so a live MCP access token presented that way is reported revoked and stays live — the very pattern the card was filed against. The repair is inside this module's own `invalid_request` branch (verify the presented token through `verifyClaims` before converting that refusal to a 200, and act on a same-client match as the `unsupported_token_type` branch does), with a leg beside the existing hint matrix. A further item is with the owner seat; detail is in the seat's reply, not here.
- `auth-manager-mcp-access-token.ts` — the split into `verifyMcpAccessTokenClaims` (unchanged checks, now answering `iat`) and `verifyMcpAccessToken` (claims then consent) is clean; the revoke door verifying through the claims half alone is necessary (it must find the grant of a token whose consent is already gone) and safe (it never admits anything). Fail-closed on every branch, including `getAuthContext` throwing.
- `auth-manager-request-routing.ts` — the request is cloned before the vendor consumes the body and only on `POST /oauth2/revoke`; the wrap is placed after the provider's answer, as the ruling and the module header require; no other route changes.
- `auth-manager.ts` — the host picks add exactly the members the bodies read; `answerOAuthTokenRevocation` is private; the revocation note now states the rule (Acceptance, last bullet). The `ipMatchesRange` region is untouched.
- `mcp-token-revocation.test.ts` — a real provider over a real engine, driven through `handleRequest`, pins every Acceptance bullet: ⭐ revoke with `client_id` only → 200 and the bearer refused, consent and refresh rows gone, refresh grant 400, consent page again; `delete-consent` → refused; another client → 200 and the owner's token works; invalid token under every hint → 200; consent-read store error → refused with a green control; delete store error → 500 then a retry 200; `skip_consent` → admitted with no row and `unsupported_token_type` kept; the description list pinned against the installed dist. The 401 at the MCP route is pinned in `@objectstack/runtime` `http-dispatcher.mcp-oauth.test.ts` on main ("invalid/expired JWT bearer → 401"), which the resolver read confirms. The ablation table in the PR body is consistent with these legs; not re-run here.
- `auth-manager.mcp-oauth.test.ts` and the three rigs — exactly-one-read, same-second admission, organization and client/user scoping, `skip_consent`, store error, no adapter, no `azp`, unreadable `createdAt`, no `iat`; the rigs now give the verifier the running server's `$context` or a real consent row, so their existing legs read the new rule rather than bypass it. The keyring rig's note that the jwt plugin stamps no `iat` unless the payload names one is true of `signJWT`, and the provider's own mint always names one — checked in the dist.

Should-fix (not blocking on their own): the 500 → 503 shape on a revoke store error (①); the owner seat filing (c) as a card.

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `36d3a9fd823694d741e71173b38c783753ffdaaf`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/mcp-token-revocation.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-mcp-access-token.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-request-routing.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/mcp-token-revocation.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.mcp-oauth.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.mcp-verifier-keyring.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.mcp-oauth-resource.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.oauth-consent-organization.test.ts + packages/spec/src/contracts/auth-service.ts (`verifyMcpAccessToken`, main), packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.ts, packages/runtime/src/security/oauth-subject-ban.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-plugin-list.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/objectql-adapter.ts and packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-actor-attribution.ts (main's merged changes to the adapter the revoke writes through), `@better-auth/oauth-provider` 1.7.12 dist (`revokeEndpoint`, `revokeJwtAccessToken`, `revokeAccessToken`, `revokeRefreshToken`, `extractClientCredentials`, `findConsent`, `invalidateRefreshFamily`, the consent endpoints, the consent write, the access-token mint), `@better-auth/core` 1.7.12 `decodeBasicCredentials`. Delta reviewed: `842d17a53a..36d3a9fd82` — one fix commit (`49868b3174`: `mcp-token-revocation.ts`, its test, the changeset) and a merge of `origin/main` at `d55acb7828`; the merge base is now `d55acb7828`. Check-runs on the head at the time of this record: 52, all completed; every conclusion `success` or `skipped` (the UI contexts skipped by paths filter), none `failure`. `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Build Core`, `Test Core` (8 shards), `TypeScript Type Check`, `Lint & Repo Gates` all `success`. ### ① Derived judgments

Delta only; the rest stands as recorded at `842d17a53a`.

- **The hinted path (the previous record's must-fix) — closed.** A provider `400 invalid_request` with an unknown-token description is no longer answered 200 outright. The wrap now reads the form token and runs `verifyClaims` on it first, whatever the hint said, and only a token that is not an MCP access token of this deployment is answered 200 as unknown (RFC 7009 §2.2). A verified token then takes exactly the `unsupported_token_type` branch's three outcomes: `azp` equal to the authenticated client → consent for (client, user, organization) and the client's refresh family deleted, 200; another client → 200 touching nothing; a `skip_consent` client → `400 unsupported_token_type`. Right: RFC 7009 §2.1 ("a hint that does not locate the token … MUST extend its search across all of its supported token types"), ruling step 1 (an MCP JWT access token presented at the revoke door is verified and acted on), step 4 kept for genuinely unknown tokens. The provider has authenticated the client before any of its unknown-token descriptions can be emitted (`revokeEndpoint`: `validateClientCredentials` precedes every token lookup), so the wrap still authenticates nobody. Pinned end to end on the real provider: live token under the other hint → 200, the verifier refuses it, consent and refresh rows gone; another client under the same hint → 200 and the owner's token works.
- **Unreadable client id → the provider's own 400 passes through** (new in this round for the hinted path; already so on the `unsupported_token_type` path). Sound, and the right side to err on: the wrap's rule is now "never a 200 that claims a revoke that did not happen", and a 400 is one the client reads as not revoked. Reachable only through a credential shape the wrap cannot read the provider's way (an extension assertion type, a non-Basic scheme), which the provider has nonetheless authenticated — the honest answer for a token the wrap can see but cannot attribute.
- **Constructed `400 unsupported_token_type` for a `skip_consent` client under another hint.** Sound: it is the answer the provider itself gives the same token with no hint or the access hint, so the client's view of that client's tokens is hint-independent; the body carries `cache-control: no-store` (RFC 6749 §5.2). Word-for-word: the test compares the constructed answer to the provider's live answer in the same run (`toEqual` on status and JSON body), and the description string is also the dist pin's positive control, so a provider rewording reds the suite rather than leaving two spellings in flight. - **A request body the wrap cannot read as a form** (not `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, or unreadable) is now answered as a token unknown to the provider → 200 when the provider said unknown, else the provider's answer. Should-fix, not blocking: on the same "never a 200 that claims a revoke that did not happen" rule, a body the wrap could not inspect at all would better pass the provider's answer through than be answered as unknown. RFC 7009 §2.1 mandates the form encoding, so the shape is outside the protocol and the measured client never sends it; recorded for the owner seat, not a ruling-A gap.
- **Merge of `origin/main` (`d55acb7828`).** Of the PR's ten files the merge changed only `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts`, by main's own one-line `resolveActor` return type (`impersonatedBy?`), far from the PR's regions; no conflict resolution touched a PR hunk. Interaction checked: main's `objectql-adapter.ts` now routes every better-auth-owned write through `authSystemWriteContext()`, which the revoke's consent and refresh-family deletes (through `$context.adapter`) also pass; with no attributed actor on a revoke request it yields `{ isSystem: true }`, the same posture as before. `auth-plugin.ts` and `auth-actor-attribution.ts` changes do not reach the verifier or the revoke wrap. No further interaction.

Public surface: unchanged (`oauthError` is module-local; nothing new reaches the package entry).

### ② Semver level

Unchanged: `@objectstack/plugin-auth` `patch`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, BREAKING banner, one ADR-0087 marker; PR body and changeset identical on the lines. The changeset's revoke paragraph now states the hint rule (RFC 7009 §2.1) and the 503 (RFC 7009 §2.2.1), matching the tree. The arm judgment of the previous record holds: the refusals removed are mis-refusals the governing text negates, cited; the one shrinking surface is the MCP door, carried by `(narrowing)`.

### ③ Boundary flags

(a) 401 vs 503 at the MCP door on a consent-store outage, (b) the refresh family deleted per (client, user) across organizations, (c) `update-consent` scope narrowing not ending minted tokens — unchanged in the tree and answered in the previous record: (a) within the ruling and the contract, escalated to the maintainer as the PR body does; (b) the ruled step 1 verbatim and the provider's own family rule, an accepted cost; (c) outside ruling A, not a contract breach, for the owner seat to file as its own card. Nothing in this round moves any of the three.

The PR body as patched opens with the seat signature line, then `Fixes #30345`, then the three declaration lines at line start; the new passages describe the hint rule and the 503 at rule level, with RFC citations and no request recipe; its ablation table adds the A3 reading for this round. The Acceptance notes still carry (a)–(c). Nothing in the public text goes below rule level.

### ④ Design judgment

- `mcp-token-revocation.ts` — the two provider answers the wrap acts on now converge on one search: verify the presented token, attribute it, act.
